correctness.rationale: The polar inverse \(Q_t(\theta)=\theta+\arcsin(t\sin\theta)\) is exact; uniform round area has polar density \(\sin^{d-1}\theta/I_d\). The deficit recurrence is \(r_{j+1}=r_j-\arcsin((1-\delta)\sin r_j)\). The first nonresonant deficit is \((-\tan\alpha)\delta\), whereas at the angular boundary it is \((\sqrt{z^2+2}-z)\sqrt\delta\). The exact mean-value identity gives one further factor of \(\delta\) at each fixed iterate, and the cap volume is asymptotic to \(A_d r^d\). Boundaries and quantifiers are explicit. The actual checker.py passed high-precision tests; finite experiments are not used as proof of infinite limits.

value.rationale: The 2022 literature motivates nonlinear normalized affine dynamics on higher spheres; a centered cap is the natural basin-neighborhood target and area-survival is its natural metric observable. At the singular homeomorphism threshold, qualitative attraction is not enough to determine survival rarity. The theorem classifies all dyadic angular resonances, explicitly identifies a half-order power shift, and resolves a universal square-root crossover with an exact coefficient. This is a motivated singular dynamics phase diagram rather than a generic change of notation or a recomputed known table.
